sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Slane is an Irish hero and a place of the old religion. He was a leader of the Fir Bolg, the people whom the Tuatha Dé Danann came to defeat. Slane was not a tall name in the tales, yet the hill that bears his name is famous. The hill of Slane stands above the bend of the River Boyne and looks out over the mounds of Brú na Bóinne. It was on that hill that St Patrick set a fire for Beltane. The king of the land saw the flame and came to the place. The fire turned the region toward the new faith. The hill that once held the hero of the Fir Bolg became the hill that held the turning of the country, so the name of Slane joins the older warrior to the saint who carried the new word.
